explanation: Searched Mathlib's valuation files (RingTheory/Valuation/: ValuationSubring.lean, Extension.lean, IsTrivialOn.lean, Integers.lean, RankOne.lean, ValuativeRel/*.lean, LocalSubring.lean) and grepped broadly for `comap_ne_top`, `comap ... = ⊤`, `IsNontrivial` correlated with `comap`/`IsAlgebraic`, and `IsAlgebraic` correlated with `Valuation`/`IsTrivialOn`/`Transcendental`. Mathlib has `ValuationSubring.comap`, `ValuationSubring.eq_top_iff` (`A = ⊤ ↔ ¬ A.valuation.IsNontrivial`), `Valuation.IsNontrivial_iff_exists_one_lt`, `Valuation.IsTrivialOn.of_le_one`, and `Valuation.transcendental_of_ne_one`, but no statement that the pullback of a proper valuation subring along an algebraic field extension is proper (equivalently, that an algebraic extension admits no nontrivial valuation trivial on the base). Deriving the target from these would require the substantive argument (some element outside Q is transcendental, contradiction), i.e. essentially the whole existing proof, so this is not a duplicate nor a one-line special case.
